result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.bfs_layers()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Group nodes by their hop distance from one or more sources. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L47741-L47803){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.bfs_layers( sources, mode="out", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![BFS layers](/assets/graphs/bfs-layers.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="An eight-node graph searched from two sources at opposite ends, A and H. Each node is colored by its hop distance to the nearer source: A and H form layer 0 (accent), B, C, F, G layer 1 (teal), and D, E, where the two searches meet, layer 2 (violet). The card lists the three layers." width="100%"} Layer 0 holds the sources, layer 1 every node one hop away, layer 2 the nodes first reached at two hops, and so on: the rings a breadth-first search explores. With several sources, each node lands in the layer of its distance to the *nearest* source. Layers are useful for drawing a graph in concentric levels, for "friends of friends" style queries (layer 2), and as a fast, unweighted counterpart of `multi_source_shortest_path_length()`. Nodes that cannot be reached appear in no layer. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, list[Union[int, str]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One starting node or a list of them, as integer IDs or string labels. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which way to follow edges on a directed graph: `"out"` (default), `"in"`, or `"all"`. Ignored for undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The layers in order, each listing node IDs in discovery order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist or `mode=` is invalid. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} From one end of a path, each layer holds one node; from both ends, the layers meet in the middle: ::: {#47956f8c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(6) path.bfs_layers(1), path.bfs_layers([1, 6]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([[1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6]], [[1, 6], [2, 5], [3, 4]]) ``` ::: :::
